newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine commercial banks' resources up 34 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine commercial banks' resources up 34 pct.

text.p: Total assets of Philippine commercial banks rose 34 percent in January to 1.932 trillion pesos from 1.440 trillion a year ago due to capital build-up and expansion of network, the Central Bank said on Monday.
Assets of foreign banks grew by 6.6 percent while assets of domestic commercial banks grew 5.7 percent.
"The growth in resources was manifested mainly in the expansion of loan portfolio by 15.3 billion pesos or 1.3 percent as other asset accounts followed a downtrend," the bank said in a statement.
As a result, industry past due loan ratio inched up to three percent from 2.8 percent a month earlier, but the Central Bank said the level remained "satisfactory".
Investment accounts of banks shrank by 0.8 percent, while cash and due from banks went down by 2.5 percent.
Deposit liabilities rose by 24.5 percent to 1.151 billion pesos. Peso deposit savings rose by 53.7 percent, while foreign currency time deposit, 26.5 percent.
Networth to risk assets ratio increased to 17 percent from 16.6 percent in end-December, higher than the minimum 10 percent statutory ratio level.
